I apologize for the issues with the search function. Let me analyze each option based on general principles of X-ray crystallography:

A. Conducting data collection at low temperatures:
Low temperatures reduce thermal motion of atoms in the crystal, which typically improves the quality of diffraction data by reducing thermal diffuse scattering and allowing more precise determination of atomic positions. This generally enhances accuracy.

B. Extending the maximum Bragg angle for data collection:
Collecting data at higher Bragg angles (higher resolution) provides more diffraction data points and allows for better resolution of atomic positions. This typically improves the accuracy of the crystal structure determination.

C. Measuring symmetry-equivalent reflections in addition to the unique data set:
Collecting redundant data (symmetry-equivalent reflections) allows for averaging of measurements, which helps identify and reduce random errors, improving the overall accuracy and reliability of the data.

D. Shortening the total X-ray exposure duration:
While shorter exposure times can reduce radiation damage to sensitive samples, they generally result in weaker diffraction signals and poorer counting statistics, which can reduce the accuracy of the data. Longer exposure times (up to a point) typically provide better signal-to-noise ratios and more accurate intensity measurements.

Based on this analysis, shortening the X-ray exposure duration (option D) would be the least likely to enhance the accuracy of diffraction data, as it typically results in weaker signals and poorer statistics, potentially reducing the quality of the data.

Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
